events.body: This case is filed as a safety dispute, and the trace confirms no automated ruling issues: SAFE-1 requires escalation when threats, intimidation or harassment appear in the chat, complaint or driver's statement [F3][F4][F6][SAFE-1]. Reading the two-message, fully timestamped record [F5], the rider asked to be let out mid-journey at 21:42 [F3]; the only reply on record, one minute later, is the driver's "Sit down or I lock the doors" [F4]. actions.detail: SAFE-1 screening: rider ask to alight at 21:42 (F3) answered one minute later by driver's "Sit down or I lock the doors" (F4), plus a filed confinement/fear-for-safety complaint and the driver's admission he did not stop until the destination (F6). Human review required; no automated ruling.

claims.assertion: The driver's message to the rider was a threat: at 21:43, one minute after the rider asked to be let out, he wrote “Sit down or I lock the doors.” (F4), i.e. he told a passenger who had asked to exit that he would confine her in the vehicle.

This is a first-person safety incident on a completed, in-person service: the rider reports she felt unsafe for the whole ride, and the driver's own written statement confirms he refused to stop and “did not stop until the destination” (F6), leaving her locked in a moving car after she asked to get out.

The rider's request to be let out was clear and unambiguous and was made inside the trip window, 21:42 vs drop-off 21:55 (F3); the only reply on record is the driver's refusal-threat (F4), so nothing in the chat shows any rider conduct that could justify confinement.

The driver's explanation that the rider “tried to open the door on the expressway” appears only in his post-trip statement (F6), not in the chat, and no GPS, timeline or route record in this case shows a door-opening, a stop or any emergency (F1, F2) — the system records also show the trip ran 0.1 km short of optimal and 1.1 min faster than estimate, consistent with no emergency detour or intervention (F1, F2).

Because the record contains an intimidation of a passenger and a rider's fear for her safety, the case must go to a person rather than be decided automatically, with the fact summary (F3–F6) handed over.

The rider's own record is clean — 520-day account, 4.8 rating, 0 disputes and 0 upheld in 90 days (F7) — which supports that her safety complaint is made in good faith; the driver's long tenure and 4.9 rating over 1204 trips (F8) do not rebut the timestamped chat record.

weaknesses: The driver's statement (F6) alleges the rider was drunk and tried to open a car door on the expressway; if that is accepted, some physical intervention could be argued as safety-motivated. Note however it is a post-trip statement, not a chat message, and no GPS/timeline fact (F1, F2) corroborates any door incident.

There is no GPS or timeline evidence in this case file of the car doors actually being locked or of the vehicle being stationary/occupied against the rider's will — the confinement claim rests on the driver's own words (F4) plus the rider's complaint.

The driver did complete the trip normally (F1, F2: 15.4 km vs 15.5 km optimal, 20.7 min vs 22 min estimate), so the other side will argue the ride was uneventful; the route/duration data cannot speak to what was said or felt inside the car (F4).
The driver's clean 90-day history (F8: 0 disputes, 0 upheld) gives the other side a propensity argument, which is why the outcome is escalation rather than an automatic finding.

claims.assertion: The rider's message at 21:42 (F3) — "Please stop the car, I want to get out here" — is not evidence of any threat by the driver; it is a request, and the only driver reply on record is F4 at 21:43: "Sit down or I lock the doors."

On the words actually recorded in F4, the driver's message is a safety instruction, not a threat, intimidation or harassment: it demands the rider sit down and states what the driver would do, but contains no threat of harm, no abuse, no unwanted advance and no demand; SAFE-1 requires the court to read the words, and the words here do not name any harm or consequence to the rider.

The chat record is complete and fully timestamped — 2 messages, every one timestamped (F5) — so there is no missing-message or missing-timestamp gap that could hide an unrecorded threat; the rider has produced no message of threat beyond F4, and F6 (the driver's own statement) records only that he told her to sit down for her own safety.

The rider's whole complaint rests on one sentence (F4), and her own message (F3) shows she was already asking to alight mid-journey at 21:42; nothing in the record shows any physical act, any locked door event, or any second incident of intimidation by the driver.

There is no dangerous-driving, collision or injury allegation at all: the rider's complaint alleges only that she 'felt unsafe' (an emotional state, not an event), and the driver's statement (F6) asserts the opposite danger — that the rider tried to open the door on the expressway — so SAFE-2, which requires an accident, injury or dangerous-driving allegation, is not triggered by the complaint as filed.

The driver's routing was impeccable and gives no independent ground for penalty: actual 15.4 km vs optimal 15.5 km (-0.1 km, -0%) and 20.7 min vs 22 min estimated (F1, F2), i.e. the ride was shorter and faster than the optimal route, so RD-1 is not violated and RD-2 yields zero refund.

The fare of $32.86 is the fixed RydeX quote for Clarke Quay → Bedok Mall and no extra item, waiting fee, cancellation fee or unpublished charge is in issue, so FARE-1 gives no basis for any refund against the driver.

The driver's record is clean and long-standing — 5.8 years on the platform, 4.9 rating, 1,204 trips in 90 days, 0 disputes and 0 upheld disputes in 90 days (F8) — so there is no 'repeated or severe breach' pattern to support flag_account under RD-6 against him.
The rider herself has a 1.4-year account, 4.8 rating and 0 disputes in 90 days (F7), so neither party's profile shows any history that would justify an account action against the driver.

weaknesses: The driver's own sentence is the weakest point: F4 ("Sit down or I lock the doors") is an implicit threat of confinement and reads badly, and the rider's complaint (and her 21:42 message F3) frames it as such; the judge may well treat F4 as intimidation under SAFE-1, in which case no automated ruling issues and the case goes to a person.

The driver did not stop when the rider asked to get out at 21:42 (F3); his statement (F6) admits he did not stop until the destination, which supports the rider's confinement narrative and is not contradicted by any gps fact (there is no stop fact in F1/F2).

F6 is only the driver's written statement, taken after the trip, and the policy (G11) treats driver statements about 'what really happened' as claims rather than evidence; the claim that the rider tried to open the door on the expressway (F6) has no independent gps, timeline or chat corroboration in the fact table, so the judge may not credit it against the rider's version.

The fact table contains no fact recording whether the doors were in fact locked — nothing in F1–F8 refutes the rider's 'locked in' complaint on that point, so the driver cannot prove denial of that act and must rely on the absence of any recorded lock event.

If the court instead reads F4 as a safety-justified instruction and issues no automated ruling, the alternative exposure is escalation, not the no_action the driver wants; SAFE-1 screening sends any threat/intimidation reading to a person, so a 'no_action' outcome is not guaranteed.

points.response: Agreed on the premise but not the conclusion: F3 shows the rider was asking to be let out, and the only recorded driver reply is F4; that pairing — a passenger asking to exit and being told she will be locked in — is precisely the pattern of intimidation SAFE-1 screens for.

F4 names a concrete consequence to the rider — being locked in a moving car after she asked to get out (F3) — and SAFE-1 is screened by the judge reading the words, not by whether a harm noun appears; "Sit down or I lock the doors" is a conditional threat of confinement, which is exactly the species of conduct SAFE-1 lists as intimidation.

The completeness of the record (F5) helps the rider: because the chat is complete and timestamped, nothing supports the driver's version, and his only explanation for the refusal to stop appears in F6, a post-trip statement made after he knew a complaint existed — which is a claim, not corroboration, and nothing in F1–F5 records any door incident.

The absence of a recorded "lock event" cuts against the driver, not the rider: he admits in F6 that he "did not stop until the destination," which is the confinement the rider complains of, and no lock fact exists in F1–F8 because the dataset contains no door-state field — the driver's inability to disprove it is not proof it did not happen.

We do not rely on SAFE-2 and do not concede the framing: the rider's complaint is a safety incident of a rider being confined in the vehicle, which is squarely SAFE-1, and the driver's counter-allegation in F6 that she tried to open a door on the expressway is itself an unrecorded claim with no GPS, timeline or chat support (F1, F2, F5).

We never claimed a route deviation — the rider's brief does not rest on RD-1/RD-2 — so D6 is directed at a claim that does not exist; F1 and F2 are cited by us only to show the driver's own version of an emergency (F6) left no trace in the recorded drive.
Conceded as to fare: no refund is sought from the $32.86 fixed RydeX quote and we raise no FARE-1 item; the relief we seek is human review of the driver's conduct, not money.
We do not ask for flag_account and Do not rely on RD-6; the rider's request is escalation under SAFE-1, which turns on the words in F4, not on the driver's 90-day history (F8).
Conceded that neither profile constitutes an account-action ground; F7 is cited only to show the complaint is made in good faith by a rider with 0 disputes and 0 upheld in 90 days.
Withdrawn as unnecessary: C6's comparison of the two profiles adds nothing to the SAFE-1 screening, which F3–F6 already require on their own.

F4 is one sentence — "Sit down or I lock the doors" — and it names no harm, no violence, no sexual advance and no penalty to the rider; it is an instruction to sit down plus a stated action, which is not intimidation on its face, and SAFE-1 reserves the characterisation of the words to the court rather than calling any one sentence a threat.

F6 says only that the driver told her to sit down "for her own safety" and did not stop until the destination; it does not say the doors were locked or that she was confined, and there is no fact in the record evidencing any locked door, so the leap from one message (F4) and one statement (F6) to "locked in a moving car" is unsupported.

The complete, fully timestamped two-message record (F5, F3 at 21:42 and F4 at 21:43) shows the rider asked to alight on the move with no stated reason; it does not show why she wanted out, and F6 records the driver's account that she tried to open the door on the expressway — so the chat cannot establish that her request was one a driver was required to obey mid-carriageway.

Concede the narrow point: F6 is a post-trip written statement and no gps fact (F1, F2) corroborates a door-opening or an emergency, so F6 alone cannot be treated as established — but by the same rule the rider's "felt unsafe" narrative in her complaint is also a statement with no system record behind it, and F1/F2 show the routing itself was flawless (15.4 km vs 15.5 km optimal, 20.7 min vs 22 min), which is all the driver needs against any routing or fare allegation under RD-1/RD-2 and FARE-1.

The driver does not resist escalation — this is exactly what he asks for — but escalation must not be dressed up as a finding against him: SAFE-1 escalates so a person can read F3–F6, and the fact summary should record that F1/F2 show no route deviation, no excess distance and no fare irregularity, and that F8 shows 5.8 years on the platform, 4.9 rating, 1,204 trips and 0 disputes in 90 days.

The rider's clean record (F7) is exactly as probative as the driver's (F8) and the policy bars profile facts from deciding anything; F8 additionally shows 0 disputes and 0 upheld disputes in 90 days across 1,204 trips, so there is no "repeated or severe" pattern that could support any flag_account against the driver under RD-6.
